ingredients.name: Long beans (yard-long beans / ma karal)
ingredients.notes: stringed and cut into 3-4cm pieces; regular green beans (sl_030 style) can substitute

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: a splash, only if needed to prevent sticking

steps.instruction: String the long beans if needed, then cut into 3-4cm pieces at a slight angle.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add curry leaves, pandan leaf, and cinnamon stick, and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the sliced onion, garlic, green chillies, and fenugreek (if using). Saute until the onion softens, about 3 minutes.
Add the chopped tomato and cook until it softens into the base, about 2 minutes.
Add the long beans, chilli powder, turmeric, curry powder, Maldive fish flakes (if using), and salt. Toss to coat the beans well. Add a splash of water if the pan looks dry.
Cover and cook over medium heat for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beans are tender but still hold their shape and a slight bite remains.
Pour in the thick coconut milk. Stir and simmer uncovered for 2-3 minutes until the sauce coats the beans and thickens slightly. Taste and adjust salt. Serve with rice.

source_site: foodcnr.com, cross-checked against islandsmile.org, srilankancookeryclass.blogspot.com, infolanka.com, thepeppercook.com, srilankanfood.weebly.com, saveur.com, and abowlofsugar.com
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 8+ independent sources; strong agreement on temper-then-add-beans technique and the thin-then-thick coconut milk approach
notes: Ma karal (yard-long beans, snake beans) are closely related to regular green beans but have a slightly firmer texture and earthier flavour that holds up well to longer cooking times. Unlike green bean curry (sl_030) which emphasises staying bright and crisp-tender, long bean curry is traditionally cooked a little longer until fully tender; the beans are robust enough not to turn mushy. The tomato base is a common addition that distinguishes the village-style version from the simpler islandsmile.org style which uses no tomato. Maldive fish flakes add the classic umami depth; omit for a fully vegan version. Regular green beans are an acceptable substitute if long beans are unavailable.
